name: Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān ibn al-Faḍl
summary: The youngest of the three Akhfashes, a student of both al-Mubarrad and Thaʿlab, who taught in Egypt and Baghdad and handed on the defence of Sībawayh in the masʾala zunbūriyya.
bio: ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān learnt from al-Mubarrad and from Thaʿlab, and from Thaʿlab's rival school as much as from his own; al-Zubaydī counts him among the companions of al-Mubarrad in the ninth Basran generation, while others count him a Kufan. He went to Egypt around 287/900 and taught there for some years, then in Aleppo, and came back to Baghdad.

Al-Zubaydī quotes him in Sībawayh's entry: Sībawayh's followers, he says, have always held that 'lo, it is he' (fa-idhā huwa hiya) is the answer, since iyyāhā could only be a ḥāl, and a ḥāl must be indefinite. The sources say he died poor in Baghdad in 315/927.
uncertain: His death is given as 315/927 or 316/928.

sources.title: al-Zubaydī, Ṭabaqāt al-naḥwiyyīn wa-l-lughawiyyīn, entry 42 (Arabic text, OpenITI)
